Subject (in full) List of Korean Political and Semi-Political
Organizations

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Grubb

Attached is a list of Korean political and
semi-political organizations in Shanghai, together with
the names of the principal executives. Office Assistant
Kim obtained the data for this list.

A. Grubb
C. D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

Please file.
J.W.S.

特科，
1935年4月1日。

S. 1

请与办公助理 Kim 合作，编制一份上海朝鲜政治及半政治组织的表格清单，并按如下指示提供详细信息：

组织名称及地址        成员人数        主要负责人姓名        组织宗旨及备注

page_data.en:
List of Korean Political and Semi-Political Organizations | Name and Address of Organization | Number of Adherants | Names of Principal Officers | Objects of Organization and Remarks | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1. Korean Provisional Government

Being a revolutionary organ its location is kept very secret and moves from one place to another as occasion demands. | Majority of Korean residents in the French Concession and Chinese controlled territory (about 1,000) | Song Byung Zo (宋秉祚), Chairman of the Political Committee.

Pak Chang Se (朴昌世), Chief of Police.

Cho Wan Ku (趙皖九), Chairman of the Law Committee.

Cho So Ang (趙素昂), Chairman of the Foreign Committee.

Kim Do Bong (金枓奉), Education Committee. | Organized in April 1919 in the French Concession by the leaders of Korean revolutionists with the object of overthrowing the Japanese administration of Korea. | | 2. Korean Independence Party.

Some times located in the French Concession and some times in Nantao. | About 40 leaders of Korean revolutionists. | Song Byung Zo (宋秉祚), President. | Organized in 1930 with the object of uniting all parties favouring independence for Korea at home and abroad and generally promoting the cause of Korean emancipation. It has branches in Peiping, Nanking and Canton. | | 3. Korean Volunteer Police Corps.

Some times established in the French Concession and some times in Nantao. | About 10 members. | Pak Chang Se (朴昌世), Chief of the Corps. | Organized in 1922 by ex-police officers of the Korean Provisional Government to guard the Provisional Government against detection by the Japanese Police. |

作为一个革命机构，其地点保密极严，并视情况需要频繁转移。 | 法租界及中国管辖区域内的大部分朝鲜居民（约1,000人） | 宋秉祚 (Song Byung Zo)，政治委员会委员长。

朴昌世 (Pak Chang Se)，警察厅长。

趙皖九 (Cho Wan Ku)，法律委员会委员长。

趙素昂 (Cho So Ang)，外交委员会委员长。

金枓奉 (Kim Do Bong)，教育委员会。 | 1919年4月由朝鲜革命领导人在法租界组建，旨在推翻日本对朝鲜的统治。 | | 2. 韩国独立党。

有时位于法租界，有时位于南市。 | 约40名朝鲜革命领导人。 | 宋秉祚 (Song Byung Zo)，总裁。 | 成立于1930年，旨在团结国内外所有赞成朝鲜独立的党派，并普遍推动朝鲜解放事业。该党在北平、南京和广州设有分部。 | | 3. 朝鲜志愿警察队。

有时设立于法租界，有时设立于南市。 | 约10名成员。 | 朴昌世 (Pak Chang Se)，队长。 | 1922年由大韩民国临时政府的前警官组建，旨在保护临时政府免受日本警察的侦测。 |
